newsitem.title: USA: US gold industry breakeven price $308/oz - report.
newsitem.headline: US gold industry breakeven price $308/oz - report.

text.p: A gold price above $308 an ounce, based on 1995 cash and non-cash costs, is necessary for the U.S. gold mining industry to break even, the U.S. Gold Institute said in a report issued Monday.

"From an economic perspective, however, at a price of $308 an ounce, the industry would not be able to cover its non-production costs such as exploration and development," the report's author John Dobra said.
At the end of 1995 the spot price of gold was around $386 per ounce, compared to around $340 Monday.

Average total cash costs - extraction, processing, administration, royalties and taxes - for the U.S. gold mining industry were around $256 an ounce in 1995, but were expected to decline to around $234 an ounce in 1996, Dobra said.
Total cash costs in 1995 were the highest since 1991 and were up 10 percent on 1994.
But extraction costs were expected to fall in 1996 as stripping was completed at a number of large and expanding surface mines, and initial work was completed at underground mines, the report said.

Seven U.S. mines, with total gold output of 4.3 million ounces, or about 40 percent of U.S. gold production, have cash costs below $250, while another 10 mines with output of 1.83 million ounces had cash costs between $250-$300 an ounce, Dobra said.
The remaining five mines surveyed had cash costs over $300 an ounce and two of these had costs over $400 an ounce, but these five high cost mines produced only about 730,000 ounces of gold in 1995.
